components.note: 亻 (person) — 体 (simplified from 體) relates to the human body.
本 (běn) is close in sound to 体's reading tǐ, sharing the same vowel though the initial has shifted over time.
力 depicts the blade of a plow — since plowing fields took great physical effort, the shape came to represent strength or power.

example.hanzi: 长途搬运需要很大的体力。
example.pinyin: Chángtú bānyùn xūyào hěn dà de tǐlì.
example.english: Long-distance moving requires a lot of physical strength.
example.fact: Leafcutter ants can carry loads up to 50 times their own body weight back to the colony, a feat of relative strength far beyond what any human could match pound for pound. Their strong mandibles let them slice through tough plant leaves, which they carry not to eat directly but to cultivate a fungus garden underground that becomes their true food source.

components.note: 攵 (an action/to strike) — ties to 致's sense of bringing about or causing an effect
至 (zhì) gives the sound — 致 is also pronounced zhì, an exact match
匕 (a kneeling person) — a mourner bowed down in grief.
歹 (skeletal remains) — the corpse being mourned, the source of 死's meaning 'to die, dead.'

example.hanzi: 这种毒蛇的毒液足以致死。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng dúshé de dúyè zúyǐ zhìsǐ.
example.english: This snake's venom is potent enough to be lethal.
example.fact: The inland taipan of Australia has venom so potent that a single bite carries enough toxin to kill roughly 100 grown men, making it the most venomous land snake known. Despite this, it is a shy, reclusive animal, and no verified human deaths have been recorded from it, largely because antivenom research targeted it early after its danger was recognized.

components.note: 忄 (heart/mind) — 性 relates to inner nature or character.
生 (shēng) gives a hint of the sound — 性 is pronounced xìng, a related sound though the initial has shifted.
屮 (a young shoot) growing up out of 土 (earth/soil) — a picture of new life emerging from the ground.
氵 (water) — 活 relates to water flowing, a symbol of life and vitality.
舌 (shé) gives a hint of the sound — 活 is pronounced huó, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.hanzi: 压力过大会影响夫妻的性生活。
example.pinyin: Yālì guò dà huì yǐngxiǎng fūqī de xìngshēnghuó.
example.english: Excessive stress can affect a couple's sex life.
example.fact: Seahorses are one of the only animal groups where the male, not the female, carries the developing young — the female deposits eggs into a specialized brood pouch on the male's abdomen, and he carries the pregnancy to term. This unusual reproductive role reversal has made seahorses a long-standing case study in evolutionary biology.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — a strong bow that took great force to draw gave 强 its meaning 'strong, powerful.'
虫 was a different phonetic element historically; its pronunciation has shifted so far from qiáng over time that the sound link is no longer obvious.
石 (stone) — 硬 describes something as hard and firm as stone.
更 (gèng) gives a sound distantly related to yìng, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 政府对此事采取了强硬的态度。
example.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ duì cǐ shì cǎiqǔle qiángyìng de tàidù.
example.english: The government took a tough stance on the matter.
example.fact: Otto von Bismarck, Prussia's chancellor in the 1860s, pursued a deliberately hard-line foreign policy he called "Realpolitik," using calculated wars and diplomacy to unify the German states into a single empire by 1871. His uncompromising negotiating style became a model still studied in international relations today.

components.note: 一 (a line, representing a target or standard) — 正 shows a foot arriving exactly at the right mark.
止 (foot, to stop) — arriving and stopping precisely at the target gives 正 its meaning of 'correct' or 'straight.'
面 was originally a pictograph of a human face, with an outline around an eye — later broadening to mean 'face, surface, side.'

example.hanzi: 硬币的正面印着国徽。
example.pinyin: Yìngbì de zhèngmiàn yìnzhe guóhuī.
example.english: The front of the coin is printed with the national emblem.
example.fact: The United States one-cent coin featured Abraham Lincoln's portrait on its front starting in 1909, making him the first real historical figure depicted on a circulating American coin. Before that, U.S. coins used only allegorical figures like Liberty, so the Lincoln cent broke a long-standing design tradition.

components.note: 冂 depicts a boundary or border enclosing an area.
土 (earth/land) — the land enclosed within the border.
口 here depicts a well within that land — together giving 周 its early meaning of a bounded territory, and later 'circumference, week, the Zhou dynasty.'
A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.

example.hanzi: 我们周一开会讨论新项目。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen Zhōuyī kāihuì tǎolùn xīn xiàngmù.
example.english: We're having a meeting on Monday to discuss the new project.
example.fact: The seven-day week did not originate from astronomy or nature but from ancient Babylon, where each day was linked to one of the seven celestial bodies visible to the naked eye: the sun, moon, and five known planets. That system spread through the Roman Empire and still underlies the names of weekdays in many languages today.

components.note: 贝 (money) — 贴 originally referred to pawning something for money, extending to 'to stick on, to subsidize.'
占 (zhàn) is only distantly related in sound to tiē — the connection has drifted apart over time.
心 was originally a pictograph of the physical shape of a human heart, and came to represent the mind, feelings, and intention as well.

example.hanzi: 她是一个很贴心的朋友。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yí ge hěn tiēxīn de péngyou.
example.english: She is a very considerate friend.
example.fact: Studies of primate grooming behavior show that chimpanzees spend hours each day picking through each other's fur, an act that serves less to remove parasites than to build and maintain social bonds within the group. Researchers consider this kind of considerate, reciprocal care essential to how primate societies stay cohesive.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — 情 relates to feelings and emotions.
青 (qīng) gives the sound — 情 is pronounced qíng, a close match differing only in tone.
亻 (person) — 侣 names a person who accompanies another.
吕 (lǚ) gives the sound — an exact match with 侣.

example.hanzi: 公园里有很多情侣在散步。
example.pinyin: Gōngyuán lǐ yǒu hěn duō qínglǚ zài sànbù.
example.english: There are many couples walking in the park.
example.fact: Emperor penguins form pair bonds each breeding season through an elaborate courtship display of bowing and calling, and though most pairs do not stay together the following year, some individuals have been observed choosing the same partner again. Their fidelity, however brief, evolved to maximize the odds of successfully raising a single chick through the brutal Antarctic winter.

components.note: 穴 (hole/cave) — 窗 originally described an opening for light and air.
囱 (cōng) gives a sound distantly related to chuāng, having drifted apart over time.
夕 (evening, night) — divination was traditionally done in the evening.
卜 (to divine, reading cracks in bone or shell) — combined with 夕 (evening), an evening divination was for unusual or 'outside' matters, giving 外 its meaning of 'outside' or 'foreign.'

example.hanzi: 窗外下起了大雨。
example.pinyin: Chuāngwài xiàqǐle dàyǔ.
example.english: It started raining heavily outside the window.
example.fact: The heaviest rainfall ever recorded in a single day fell on Foc-Foc, Réunion Island, on January 8, 1966, when 1.825 meters (about 6 feet) of rain fell in just 24 hours during Cyclone Denise. Réunion's steep volcanic terrain repeatedly funnels moist tropical air upward, making it one of the wettest places on Earth.

components.note: 贝 (shell) — ancient Chinese currency was made from cowrie shells, linking 贝 to wealth
才 (cái) gives the sound — an exact match with 财's reading cái
宀 (a roof) — a house where valuables are kept
玉 (jade) — the treasure kept safe inside

example.hanzi: 海盗们把财宝埋在了荒岛上。
example.pinyin: Hǎidàomen bǎ cáibǎo máizàile huāngdǎo shàng.
example.english: The pirates buried the treasure on a deserted island.
example.fact: The wreck of the Spanish galleon Nuestra Señora de Atocha, sunk by a hurricane in 1622 off the Florida Keys, was located by treasure hunter Mel Fisher in 1985 after a 16-year search, yielding gold, silver, and emeralds worth over $400 million. Fisher's discovery remains one of the largest verified troves of sunken treasure ever recovered.

components.note: 囗 (a boundary/enclosure) surrounding 玉 (jade, treasure) — a country pictured as protected, valuable territory.
冂 (an enclosure or doorway) — 内 pictures the space one enters.
人 (person) — a person entering an enclosure gave 内 its meaning 'inside' or 'within.'

example.hanzi: 这家公司在国内很有名。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī zài guónèi hěn yǒumíng.
example.english: This company is very famous domestically.
example.fact: Japan's domestic bullet train network, the Shinkansen, launched in 1964 in time for the Tokyo Olympics and has operated for decades with a safety record so strong that it has never had a passenger fatality from a derailment or collision in commercial operation. Its punctuality is legendary, with average delays historically measured in seconds rather than minutes.

components.note: 阝 (a mound/city) — represents a place being traveled to.
迶 depicts walking or moving along a path — following someone to the city gave 随 its meaning 'to follow, along with.'
木 (wood) — 机 originally referred to a wooden device or machine, such as a loom.
几 depicts a small table or stool — combined with 木 (wood), the character pictured a wooden machine or mechanism.

example.hanzi: 这个软件会随机生成密码。
example.pinyin: Zhège ruǎnjiàn huì suíjī shēngchéng mìmǎ.
example.english: This software randomly generates passwords.
example.fact: True randomness is surprisingly hard for computers to produce on their own, since ordinary algorithms are deterministic; many systems instead harvest unpredictable physical phenomena, such as atmospheric noise or the precise timing of mouse movements, to seed their random number generators. Cloudflare famously uses a wall of lava lamps, filmed continuously, as one such source of physical randomness.

components.note: 土 (soil) — earth being pressed down
厂 (a cliff/overhang) — a heavy mass bearing down from above
Hand — an action done by hand, like pressing down.
Gives the sound áng, related to yì but drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 长期压抑情绪对健康不好。
example.pinyin: Chángqí yāyì qíngxù duì jiànkāng bù hǎo.
example.english: Long-term suppression of emotions is bad for health.
example.fact: Research from the University of Texas in the 1990s found that people instructed to suppress their emotional expressions during a stressful task showed a measurable rise in blood pressure compared with those who expressed emotion freely, suggesting that habitual emotional suppression carries a real physiological cost. This finding helped establish emotion regulation as a major topic in health psychology.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 知 relates to speaking what one knows.
矢 (shǐ) gives a hint of the sound — 知 is pronounced zhī, a connection that has faded over time.
见 (to see, perceive) — relates to 觉's meaning 'to feel, sense, perceive.'
⺍ is a small graphic element serving as the phonetic hint, though its link to jué's modern sound has faded after centuries of change.

example.hanzi: 病人失去知觉,被送进了医院。
example.pinyin: Bìngrén shīqù zhījué, bèi sòngjìnle yīyuàn.
example.english: The patient lost consciousness and was sent to the hospital.
example.fact: General anesthesia reliably switches off conscious perception, yet scientists still do not fully understand the mechanism by which it does so; one leading theory holds that anesthetic drugs disrupt the long-range communication between different brain regions rather than simply shutting neurons down. This gap in understanding makes anesthesia one of medicine's most widely used yet least explained tools.

components.note: 气 (simplified from 氣) depicts rising wisps or vapor, like breath or steam drifting upward — a simple picture of air or gas.
亻 (person) — 体 (simplified from 體) relates to the human body.
本 (běn) is close in sound to 体's reading tǐ, sharing the same vowel though the initial has shifted over time.

example.hanzi: 氢气是一种极轻的气体。
example.pinyin: Qīngqì shì yì zhǒng jí qīng de qìtǐ.
example.english: Hydrogen is an extremely light gas.
example.fact: Hydrogen is the lightest and most abundant element in the universe, making up roughly 75 percent of all normal matter by mass, mostly in stars where it fuels nuclear fusion. On Earth, though, free hydrogen gas is rare because it is light enough to escape the atmosphere over geological time.

components.note: 土 (earth) — relates to 城's meaning 'city, wall,' since city walls were built of earth.
成 (chéng) gives the sound — 城 is also pronounced chéng, an exact match.
钅 (metal) — 镇 originally referred to a heavy metal weight used to press something down, later extending to 'garrison town.'
真 (zhēn) gives the sound — an exact match with 镇's reading zhèn, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 这是一个风景优美的小城镇。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí ge fēngjǐng yōuměi de xiǎo chéngzhèn.
example.english: This is a small town with beautiful scenery.
example.fact: Pompeii, buried by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD, was a thriving Roman town of roughly 11,000 people before the disaster, and the volcanic ash that destroyed it also preserved streets, buildings, and even plaster casts of victims in extraordinary detail. Excavations begun in the 18th century continue today, still revealing new sections of the town.

components.note: 发 simplifies 發, which pictured 弓 (a bow) drawn back by two hands — 'to shoot forth' — later extended to 发's meaning 'to send out, issue, emit.'
火 (fire) — 烧 describes burning or cooking with fire.
尧 (yáo) gives a rhyme close to shāo, with a different initial.

example.hanzi: 孩子昨晚发烧到39度。
example.pinyin: Háizi zuówǎn fāshāo dào sānshíjiǔ dù.
example.english: The child had a fever of 39 degrees last night.
example.fact: A fever is not a malfunction but an evolved defense: raising body temperature by even one or two degrees can slow the reproduction of many bacteria and viruses while boosting the activity of immune cells. This is why doctors are often cautious about aggressively treating a mild fever, since the response itself may be helping fight the infection.

components.note: 阝 (a mound/place) — reflects 阿's original meaning related to a hill or slope
可 (kě) gives a sound close to 阿's reading ā
扌 (hand) — relates directly to 拉's meaning 'to pull, drag,' an action done by hand.
立 (lì) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted noticeably from lā.
亻 (person) — 伯 names a male relative, a person in the family.
白 (bái) gives the sound — close to bó, sharing the same initial and a similar rhyme.

example.hanzi: 阿拉伯数字被全世界广泛使用。
example.pinyin: Ālābó shùzì bèi quán shìjiè guǎngfàn shǐyòng.
example.english: Arabic numerals are widely used all over the world.
example.fact: The number system commonly called "Arabic numerals" actually originated in India and was later transmitted to Europe by Arab mathematicians and traders around the 9th to 12th centuries, which is how it acquired its Western name. The system's use of a placeholder zero and positional notation made arithmetic far simpler than the Roman numerals it eventually displaced.

components.note: 无 simplifies 無, which originally pictured a dancer holding tasseled ornaments; the character was later borrowed purely for its sound to write the unrelated word 'without, not have,' the meaning 无 carries today.
Originally a drawing of a bear, with 厶 as its head, ⺼ as its body, and 匕匕 as its claws; the picture was later borrowed to mean 'ability, to be able to.'

example.hanzi: 他因为工作无能被公司解雇了。
example.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi gōngzuò wúnéng bèi gōngsī jiěgùle.
example.english: He was fired by the company because of his incompetence at work.
example.fact: The Peter Principle, proposed by educator Laurence J. Peter in 1969, argues that employees in a hierarchy tend to be promoted based on success in their current role until they reach a position where they are no longer competent, at which point they typically stay stuck. The idea remains a widely cited, if only partly tested, explanation for organizational dysfunction.

components.note: 冫 pictures ice crystals forming.
水 (water) sits beside it, together showing water turned to ice.
氵 (water) — 激 originally described water dashing or surging forcefully
敫 (jiǎo) gives a sound distantly related to 激's reading jī, having drifted apart over time
Ice — related to the character's early sense of cold.
Gives the sound líng, matching the character's reading.

example.hanzi: 夏天孩子们最喜欢吃冰激凌。
example.pinyin: Xiàtiān háizimen zuì xǐhuan chī bīngjīlíng.
example.english: In summer, children love eating ice cream the most.
example.fact: Ice cream's ancestor may date back over 2,000 years to China, where Tang dynasty records describe a chilled dessert made of fermented milk packed in ice. The frozen dessert as we know it today only became widely affordable after mechanical refrigeration was developed in the 19th century.

components.note: 千 (thousand) — 重 pictures a heavy burden carried a great distance.
里 (a unit of distance, like a mile) — carrying something a thousand 里 emphasizes how heavy and significant a burden it is, giving 重 its meaning 'heavy' or 'important.'
见 (to see) — relates directly to 视's meaning 'to look at, view.'
礻 (a form of 示, shì) gives the sound — 视 is also pronounced shì, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 这家公司非常重视员工的健康。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī fēicháng zhòngshì yuángōng de jiànkāng.
example.english: This company places great importance on employees' health.
example.fact: Finland has consistently ranked among the top countries in international workplace well-being surveys, partly because Finnish labor law guarantees generous parental leave and mandates regular rest breaks, reflecting a national culture that places heavy institutional value on worker health. Comparative OECD studies often cite Finland alongside other Nordic countries as a benchmark for balancing productivity with well-being.

components.note: 氵 (water) — relates directly to 流's meaning 'to flow.'
㐬 (liú) gives the sound — 流 is also pronounced liú, an exact match.
氵 (water) — 浪 names movement on the surface of water, a wave.
良 (liáng) gives a rhyme close to làng, with a different initial and tone.

example.hanzi: 这只流浪狗被好心人收养了。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhī liúlàng gǒu bèi hǎoxīnrén shōuyǎngle.
example.english: This stray dog was adopted by a kind-hearted person.
example.fact: Moscow's stray dog population became famous for a small number of individuals that learned to ride the city's subway system, boarding trains at one stop and exiting closer to reliable food sources. Researchers who studied the behavior in the 2000s found the dogs used sound and scheduling cues, adapting an entirely human transit system to their own survival needs.

components.note: 宀 (roof/house) — relates to 完's meaning 'complete, finish,' as in a fully built house.
元 (yuán) was the phonetic base; the pronunciation later shifted to wán, so only a partial rhyme remains today.
Depicts a child wrapped in swaddling, related to 子 (child); the picture-meaning has nothing to do with its modern grammatical role marking a completed action or change of state.

example.hanzi: 手机掉进水里,完了。
example.pinyin: Shǒujī diàojìn shuǐ lǐ, wánle.
example.english: The phone fell into the water — it's done for.
example.fact: Most modern smartphones are not actually destroyed by water immersion itself but by the short circuits that occur afterward when the device is powered on while still wet, which is why manufacturers and repair technicians almost universally recommend leaving a soaked phone off and drying out for at least 24 hours before attempting to turn it on again.

components.note: A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.
人 (a person) — kneeling before a figure of authority, the image of receiving an order that gave 令 its meaning 'command, order; to cause.'

example.hanzi: 将军下令全军立刻撤退。
example.pinyin: Jiāngjūn xiàlìng quánjūn lìkè chètuì.
example.english: The general ordered the entire army to retreat immediately.
example.fact: In 1940, facing near-certain defeat at Dunkirk, the German high command controversially halted its advancing panzer divisions for several days, an order historians still debate the reasoning behind, which gave British and French forces time to organize the evacuation of over 330,000 troops across the English Channel.

components.note: A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.
水 depicts a flowing stream, with a central current and ripples or drops branching off to the sides.
辶 (to walk) — 道 relates to a path or road one walks along.
首 (shǒu) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading no longer resembles dào, a reminder that sound components can drift after thousands of years of pronunciation change.

example.hanzi: 城市的下水道系统需要定期维护。
example.pinyin: Chéngshì de xiàshuǐdào xìtǒng xūyào dìngqī wéihù.
example.english: The city's sewer system needs regular maintenance.
example.fact: Ancient Rome's Cloaca Maxima, built around the 6th century BC to drain marshes and carry away waste, is considered one of the world's earliest large-scale sewer systems, and parts of its stone channels still exist and function beneath modern Rome today. Its construction was a major reason the city could grow as densely as it did in antiquity.

components.note: Grass/plant — links to natural green or blue-green colors.
Gives the sound cāng, matching the character's reading.
虫 depicts an insect.
黾 depicts a toad or frog with a round body — paired with the insect, it points to a small flying pest that toads like to eat, giving 蝇 its meaning 'fly.'

example.hanzi: 厨房里飞进来一只苍蝇。
example.pinyin: Chúfáng lǐ fēijìnlái yì zhī cāngying.
example.english: A housefly flew into the kitchen.
example.fact: Houseflies can taste with receptors located on their feet, meaning they effectively sample a surface's chemistry the instant they land on it, which is part of why they seem to check out food so quickly before deciding whether to eat. Their compound eyes also process motion far faster than human eyes, letting them dodge swats that would easily catch a slower-reacting insect.

components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
⺼ (flesh/body) — part of the body.
退 (to step back, retreat) — used to move and walk, together giving 腿 its meaning 'leg.'

example.hanzi: 他跑步时大腿肌肉拉伤了。
example.pinyin: Tā pǎobù shí dàtuǐ jīròu lāshāngle.
example.english: He strained his thigh muscle while running.
example.fact: The femur, the bone running through the thigh, is the longest and strongest bone in the human body, able to withstand roughly 1,800 kilograms (about 4,000 pounds) of compressive force before fracturing under laboratory testing — several times the average adult's body weight.

components.note: 木 (tree) — 杜 names a kind of tree, the birchleaf pear.
土 (tǔ) gives a sound close to dù.
戌 (a halberd/weapon) — represents armed force.
女 (woman) — force used to intimidate gave 威 its meaning 'power, might, awe-inspiring.'

example.hanzi: 图书馆采用杜威十进分类法整理图书。
example.pinyin: Túshūguǎn cǎiyòng Dùwēi shíjìn fēnlèifǎ zhěnglǐ túshū.
example.english: The library organizes its books using the Dewey Decimal Classification.
example.fact: The Dewey Decimal System, created by American librarian Melvil Dewey in 1876, organizes library books into ten broad numbered categories that can be subdivided endlessly with decimal points, and it remains in active use in tens of thousands of libraries worldwide despite being nearly 150 years old.

components.note: 亻 (a person) — paired with speech.
言 (speech, words) — a person's spoken words were taken as trustworthy, giving 信 its meaning 'to trust, believe' and, by extension, 'a letter, message.'
⺮ (bamboo) — 箱 originally described a bamboo case or chest.
相 (xiāng) gives the sound — an exact match with 箱.

example.hanzi: 请把包裹放进信箱里。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ bāoguǒ fàngjìn xìnxiāng lǐ.
example.english: Please put the package in the mailbox.
example.fact: The color of mailboxes varies widely by country and carries historical meaning: red boxes in the United Kingdom trace back to Victorian-era standardization in the 1870s so they could be spotted easily against most backgrounds, while the blue mailboxes of the United States were adopted more recently, in 1955, replacing an older olive-green design.

components.note: 米 (grain, especially husked rice) — 精's meaning 'refined, essence, spirit' relates to rice refined to its purest form.
青 (qīng) gives a sound hint — 精 is pronounced jīng, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant differs.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 显微镜下可以看到精子的活动。
example.pinyin: Xiǎnwēijìng xià kěyǐ kàndào jīngzǐ de huódòng.
example.english: Sperm cell movement can be observed under a microscope.
example.fact: Human sperm cells are among the smallest cells in the body, yet they must travel a relatively enormous distance — roughly 15 to 18 centimeters through the female reproductive tract — a journey proportionally comparable to a human swimming several kilometers, which is one reason only a tiny fraction ever reach an egg.

components.note: 灰 depicts the leftover ash of a fire 火 below, mixed with dust — the source of its meaning 'ash, gray.'
⺈ (a person, bent over) — the figure whose outward expression is being depicted.
巴 — traditionally linked to desire or emotion, so together the character points to a person's expression or complexion, extended to 色's meaning 'color, appearance.'

example.hanzi: 天空变成了灰色,好像要下雨了。
example.pinyin: Tiānkōng biànchéngle huīsè, hǎoxiàng yào xiàyǔ le.
example.english: The sky turned gray, as if it were about to rain.
example.fact: African elephants owe part of their gray color to a thick layer of skin up to 2.5 centimeters deep that they regularly coat in dust and mud, which both protects against sunburn and helps regulate body temperature, giving their already gray hide an even duller, matted appearance in the wild.

components.note: 巴 is of disputed pictographic origin, sometimes explained as an early drawing of a large snake or reptile with a curled tail; the character was later borrowed for place names and the grammatical uses it carries today.
土 (earth) — 基 relates to the ground or foundation something is built on.
其 (qí) gives a hint of the sound — 基 is pronounced jī, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.
斤 (an axe) — 斯's original meaning was 'to split, to tear apart' with an axe.
其 (qí) is close in sound to sī, sharing a related initial though the rhyme has drifted apart over the centuries.
土 (earth) — 坦 describes flat, level ground.
旦 (dàn) gives a sound close to tǎn, sharing a related rhyme.

example.hanzi: 巴基斯坦位于南亚地区。
example.pinyin: Bājīsītǎn wèiyú Nányà dìqū.
example.english: Pakistan is located in South Asia.
example.fact: K2, the world's second-highest mountain at 8,611 meters, sits on the border between Pakistan and China and is considered far more dangerous to climb than Everest, with a historical fatality rate among summiteers of roughly one in four, earning it the nickname "Savage Mountain."

components.note: 面 was originally a pictograph of a human face, with an outline around an eye — later broadening to mean 'face, surface, side.'
又 (hand) and 寸 (also derived from a hand shape) — together suggesting two hands matching or corresponding, related to 对's meaning 'correct, matching.'
面 was originally a pictograph of a human face, with an outline around an eye — later broadening to mean 'face, surface, side.'

example.hanzi: 我们终于可以面对面交谈了。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōngyú kěyǐ miànduìmiàn jiāotán le.
example.english: We can finally talk face to face.
example.fact: Psychologists studying communication have found that face-to-face conversation conveys emotional tone through combined channels — facial expression, tone of voice, and body posture — that phone calls and text messages strip away one by one, which is part of why misunderstandings are statistically more common in text-based exchanges than in in-person conversation.

components.note: 电 (simplified from 電) depicts a bolt of lightning — since lightning is a natural form of electricity, the character came to mean 'electricity.'
手 (hand) — in the traditional form 擊, 手 contributed the meaning of striking with force, the source of 击's meaning 'to hit, strike.'

example.hanzi: 修理电线时要小心电击。
example.pinyin: Xiūlǐ diànxiàn shí yào xiǎoxīn diànjī.
example.english: Be careful of electric shock when repairing wires.
example.fact: The electric eel, despite its name actually a type of knifefish, can generate discharges of up to 860 volts, among the strongest bioelectric shocks of any animal, using thousands of specialized cells called electrocytes stacked like tiny batteries along its body to stun prey and deter predators.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 进 relates to advancing or entering, both movement-related.
井 (jǐng) gives a close sound cue — 进 is pronounced jìn, sharing similar consonant and vowel sounds.
亻 (an upright person) — paired with an inverted figure.
匕 here represents a person turned upside down — an upright figure beside an inverted one pictures transformation, giving 化 its meaning 'to change, transform.'

example.hanzi: 达尔文提出了生物进化的理论。
example.pinyin: Dá'ěrwén tíchūle shēngwù jìnhuà de lǐlùn.
example.english: Darwin proposed the theory of biological evolution.
example.fact: Charles Darwin published "On the Origin of Species" in 1859, but he had actually developed the core idea of natural selection two decades earlier, delaying publication partly out of caution over its controversial implications until a letter from fellow naturalist Alfred Russel Wallace, independently arriving at a similar theory, prompted him to finally go public.

components.note: 日 (sun) — 最 pictures something happening under the sun, that is, everywhere.
取 (to take, gather) — combined with the sun above, gathering everything under the sun gave 最 its meaning of 'most' or 'the utmost.'
氐 (dī) gives the sound — 低 is also pronounced dī, an exact match

example.hanzi: 今天的最低气温是零下五度。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān de zuìdī qìwēn shì língxià wǔ dù.
example.english: Today's lowest temperature is minus five degrees.
example.fact: The lowest natural air temperature ever recorded on Earth's surface was -89.2°C (-128.6°F), measured at the Soviet Vostok Station in Antarctica in 1983, a spot so cold and dry that exposed skin can suffer frostbite within minutes and diesel fuel would freeze solid without special additives.

components.note: 发 simplifies 發, which pictured 弓 (a bow) drawn back by two hands — 'to shoot forth' — later extended to 发's meaning 'to send out, issue, emit.'
彳 depicts a step with the left foot; together with 亍 (a step with the right foot), 行 shows a person walking or moving.
亍 depicts a step with the right foot, complementing 彳 to form the idea of walking or travel.

example.hanzi: 这本小说将于下个月正式发行。
example.pinyin: Zhè běn xiǎoshuō jiāngyú xià ge yuè zhèngshì fāxíng.
example.english: This novel will be officially published next month.
example.fact: Johannes Gutenberg's printing press, developed around 1440 in Mainz, Germany, made it possible to issue multiple identical copies of a text far faster than hand-copying, and historians estimate that within 50 years of its invention, tens of millions of books had been printed across Europe — a scale of publishing unimaginable before.

components.note: Hand — twisting is done with the hand.
Gives the sound chǒu, related to niǔ but drifted apart over time.
The outline pictures a bent, curved container or musical instrument, giving 曲 its meaning 'crooked, bent' and, by extension, 'a tune.'

example.hanzi: 强烈的磁场会扭曲指南针的方向。
example.pinyin: Qiángliè de cíchǎng huì niǔqū zhǐnánzhēn de fāngxiàng.
example.english: A strong magnetic field will distort the compass's direction.
example.fact: According to Einstein's general theory of relativity, massive objects like stars and planets actually distort the fabric of spacetime itself, bending the paths of light and nearby objects — an effect confirmed in 1919 when astronomers observed starlight curving as it passed near the sun during a solar eclipse.

components.note: 十 (ten) — 博 relates to breadth, with ten symbolizing completeness.
尃 (fū) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading bó has diverged considerably.
宀 (roof) — represents a home.
各 (each, various) — a person arriving from elsewhere and welcomed under one's roof gave 客 its meaning 'guest, visitor.'

example.hanzi: 她开了一个关于旅行的博客。
example.pinyin: Tā kāile yí ge guānyú lǜxíng de bókè.
example.english: She started a blog about traveling.
example.fact: The word "weblog" was coined in 1997 by programmer Jorn Barger, and it was later shortened to "blog" in 1999 by Peter Merholz, who split the word playfully as "we blog" in a post on his own site — a casual joke that ended up naming an entire medium.

components.note: 女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'
又 (hand), shown twice and joined together — two hands clasped in friendship gave 友 its meaning 'friend.'

example.hanzi: 他是我最好的好友。
example.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ zuì hǎo de hǎoyǒu.
example.english: He is my very best friend.
example.fact: A famous long-running Harvard study that has tracked hundreds of men since 1938 found that the strength of close personal relationships, more than wealth or fame, was the single strongest predictor of health and happiness in later life, a conclusion the study's directors have highlighted repeatedly across more than 80 years of data.

components.note: 发 simplifies 發, which pictured 弓 (a bow) drawn back by two hands — 'to shoot forth' — later extended to 发's meaning 'to send out, issue, emit.'
⺼ (flesh) — 脾 names a body organ, the spleen.
卑 (bēi) gives a sound close to pí, sharing a related initial though the rhyme has shifted.
气 (simplified from 氣) depicts rising wisps or vapor, like breath or steam drifting upward — a simple picture of air or gas.

example.hanzi: 他因为一点小事就对同事发脾气。
example.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi yìdiǎn xiǎoshì jiù duì tóngshì fāpíqi.
example.english: He lost his temper at a colleague over a trivial matter.
example.fact: Neuroscientists have found that during an angry outburst, activity in the brain's prefrontal cortex — the region responsible for impulse control and rational judgment — tends to drop while the amygdala, tied to fear and aggression, becomes more active, which helps explain why people often say things in anger they later regret.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 偷 describes a person's action, stealing.
俞 (yú) gives a sound distantly related to tōu, having drifted apart over time.
穴 (hole) — 窃 originally described sneaking through a hole to steal.
切 (qiè) gives the sound — an exact match with 窃.

example.hanzi: 商店安装了摄像头以防止偷窃。
example.pinyin: Shāngdiàn ānzhuāngle shèxiàngtóu yǐ fángzhǐ tōuqiè.
example.english: The store installed cameras to prevent theft.
example.fact: The Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum theft of 1990, in which thieves disguised as police officers stole 13 artworks worth an estimated $500 million, remains the largest unsolved art theft in history, and the museum still displays the empty frames on its walls as a standing invitation for the missing pieces' return.

components.note: 面 was originally a pictograph of a human face, with an outline around an eye — later broadening to mean 'face, surface, side.'
子 (a baby) — a small child.
乚 (a hook shape) — here representing an open, crying mouth, together giving 孔 its meaning 'hole, opening.'

example.hanzi: 多年不见,他的面孔已经变了很多。
example.pinyin: Duōnián bújiàn, tā de miànkǒng yǐjīng biànle hěn duō.
example.english: After years apart, his face had changed a lot.
example.fact: Humans are remarkably specialized at recognizing faces, relying on a dedicated brain region called the fusiform face area that activates far more strongly for faces than for almost any other visual category, which is also why humans are prone to "face pareidolia" — seeing faces in clouds, rock formations, or everyday objects.

components.note: 哥 doubles the character 可 ('to approve, to sing'), originally suggesting a call-and-response song between two singers; the meaning later narrowed to 'elder brother.'
亻 (person) — 伦 relates to human relationships and social order.
仑 depicts an orderly, logical arrangement — combined with 亻, giving 伦 its meaning 'human relationships, order.'
比 is made of two identical 匕 (spoon) shapes placed side by side — comparing two similar things led to its meaning 'to compare.'
A pictograph of a cross-shaped building, possibly an altar or temple floor plan; the character was later adopted to write 'Asia' (亚洲) and the unrelated meaning 'second, next.'

example.hanzi: 哥伦比亚是世界上咖啡产量最高的国家之一。
example.pinyin: Gēlúnbǐyà shì shìjiè shàng kāfēi chǎnliàng zuì gāo de guójiā zhīyī.
example.english: Colombia is one of the countries with the highest coffee production in the world.
example.fact: Colombia's mountainous terrain and equatorial climate give it two coffee harvests a year in many regions, unlike most coffee-growing countries that harvest only once, which is a major reason the country has remained among the world's top coffee exporters for over a century.

components.note: 羊 (sheep) — food offered generously to another person
口 (mouth) — kind words spoken alongside the gift

于 is an ancient character of disputed pictographic origin, sometimes explained as a bent stroke representing breath escaping with effort; it was borrowed early on for the grammatical sense 'at, in, to' it carries in modern usage.

example.hanzi: 她善于处理复杂的人际关系。
example.pinyin: Tā shànyú chǔlǐ fùzá de rénjì guānxi.
example.english: She is good at handling complex interpersonal relationships.
example.fact: Octopuses are famously skilled problem-solvers despite having no centralized brain structure comparable to vertebrates; roughly two-thirds of their neurons are distributed throughout their arms, letting each arm process sensory information and make some decisions independently while still coordinating with the rest of the body.

components.note: 黄 originally depicted a large ornamental jade pendant worn at the waist; the character was later borrowed for the color 'yellow.'
氵 (water) — 油 names an oily liquid.
由 (yóu) gives the sound — an exact match with 油.

example.hanzi: 妈妈在面包上涂了一层黄油。
example.pinyin: Māma zài miànbāo shàng túle yì céng huángyóu.
example.english: Mom spread a layer of butter on the bread.
example.fact: Making one pound of butter requires roughly 21 pints of milk, since butter is essentially the concentrated fat skimmed and churned out of cream, and archaeological evidence suggests humans have been churning butter for at least 4,000 years, with ancient butter remains even found preserved in Irish peat bogs.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 推 relates to pushing something with the hand
隹 (zhuī) gives a loose sound connection to 推's reading tuī
辶 (walk/movement) — 迟 describes moving too slowly, arriving 'late.'
尺 (chǐ) gives a sound very close to chí, sharing the initial and rhyme — only the tone differs.

example.hanzi: 由于天气原因,航班被推迟了。
example.pinyin: Yóuyú tiānqì yuányīn, hángbān bèi tuīchíle.
example.english: The flight was postponed due to weather conditions.
example.fact: The 2020 Tokyo Olympics were postponed by a full year, to 2021, marking the first time in the modern Games' history that an Olympics was delayed rather than outright cancelled, a decision driven by the global COVID-19 pandemic and made only about four months before the original opening ceremony.

example.hanzi: 吃完饭我们出去转转吧。
example.pinyin: Chī wán fàn wǒmen chūqù zhuànzhuan ba.
example.english: Let's go out for a stroll after we finish eating.
example.fact: A short walk after a meal has a measurable physiological benefit: several clinical studies have found that walking for just 10 to 15 minutes after eating can meaningfully lower the resulting spike in blood sugar compared with remaining seated, an effect linked to muscles absorbing glucose from the bloodstream during light activity.

components.note: 辶 (to walk, movement) — 通 relates to passing through or getting somewhere.
甬 (yǒng) gives a hint of the sound — 通 is pronounced tōng, a connection that has shifted over time.
彳 depicts a step with the left foot; together with 亍 (a step with the right foot), 行 shows a person walking or moving.

讠 (speech) — the act of speaking.
正 (straight, correct) — speaking the straight, correct truth, giving 证 its meaning 'to prove, certify; evidence.'

example.hanzi: 进入这个区域需要特别通行证。
example.pinyin: Jìnrù zhège qūyù xūyào tèbié tōngxíngzhèng.
example.english: Entering this area requires a special pass.
example.fact: During the Cold War, East German citizens needed rarely granted passes to cross into West Berlin, and when travel restrictions were unexpectedly announced as lifted on November 9, 1989, tens of thousands of people rushed the checkpoints that same night without waiting for passes at all, effectively ending the wall's control almost overnight.

components.note: 火 (fire) — 烤 describes cooking directly over fire or heat.
考 (kǎo) gives the sound — an exact match with 烤.
冂 traces the outer outline of a cut of meat.
仌 depicts the muscle fibers or ribs inside, together forming a picture of a piece of meat.

example.hanzi: 周末我们打算在院子里烤肉。
example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen dǎsuàn zài yuànzi lǐ kǎoròu.
example.english: This weekend we plan to barbecue in the yard.
example.fact: Archaeological evidence suggests early humans were cooking meat over fire at least 780,000 years ago at a site in modern-day Israel, and some researchers argue that the ability to cook food fundamentally changed human evolution by making calories easier to digest, possibly enabling the brain growth seen in later hominins.
